title: Redwood Optimize walkthrough - batching & KV cache cost model (Mariner Payments)
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Mariner Payments through Optimize recommendations around batching and prefix/KV cache. Discussed tradeoffs (latency vs cost), KV cache hit rates for repetitive prompts, cost model spreadsheet, and next steps to run a 1-week benchmark on their traffic. Security and data residency questions raised; Redwood to share SOC2, SSO/KMS docs.
next_steps: Tom to send KV cache cost model spreadsheet and sample config
Maya to share SOC2 + security packet and pricing for Dedicated pilot
Customer to provide sample traffic logs (anonymized) for 1-week bench
Schedule follow-up in 1 week to review benchmark results
action_items: Tom Reynolds - share KV cache cost model spreadsheet - due 2026-04-27
Maya Patel - send SOC2 + security docs and Dedicated pricing - due 2026-04-24
Samir Khan - export 3 days of anonymized traffic/seq-length distribution - due 2026-04-26
meeting_header: Date: 2026-04-22 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~49 minutes | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Tom Reynolds (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Mariner CTO), Samir Khan (Lead ML Eng), Priya Desai (SRE), Jorge Alvarez (Product)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we wanted to run through Redwood Optimize focused on batching and prefix / K-V cache today. Got Tom from our SE team.
[00:10] Tom: yeah hi all, quick agenda: why batching helps, how prefix/KV cache works for repeated prompts, the cost model, and then a short pilot plan.
[00:22] Lena: sounds good, our main goals are reduce cost per 1M tokens and keep tail latency under 150ms for API calls. We also have data residency constraints in EU.
[00:30] Maya: great, good to call that out up front. quick qual - are you currently calling the model through hosted OpenAI endpoints or running anything on-prem?
[00:40] Samir: we run a mix, most inference hits Vertex AI for embeddings and a few on-prem endpoints for PCI workloads. We're looking at reducing TCO and want predictable throughput for peak batch settlement windows.
[00:55] Tom: makes sense. so two levers we usually see: request batching (continuous batching in the runtime) which boosts throughput and reduces per-token GPU overhead, and the prefix/KV cache which saves tokens on repeated prefixes like standard payment reconciliation prompts.
[01:10] Priya: can you explain prefix cache again, I keep hearing K-V cash in notes, lol.
[01:15] Tom: sure, prefix cache stores the KV cache (attention + key/values) for common prefixes so you don't re-tokenize/compute the initial context. so for flows where the first 50-150 tokens are identical across requests, you get big savings.
[01:30] Samir: what's the hit rate you typically see?
[01:35] Tom: depends; for identical front-loaded prompts we see 60-90% hit rates in payment workflows in our benchmarks. when prompts vary slightly, hit rate drops, but partial prefix matching still helps.
[01:45] Lena: ok and latency impact? I worry caching might add jitter.
[01:50] Tom: good question — cache lookup is very cheap, sub-ms in our runtime. the bigger latency tradeoff is batching: larger batch windows add queueing delay. we tune batching with a max wait (e.g., 5-15ms) so you get throughput gains while keeping p95 under target.
[02:10] Maya: we prepared a cost model spreadsheet — shows token savings from cache + batching effects on throughput and GPU utilization. I sent a quick link in chat: (link: /redwood/optimize/kvcache-cost-model.xlsx)
[02:25] Jorge: I see the spreadsheet — couple numbers: baseline tokens per request 420, caching reduces average tokens to 160 with 65% hit rate, that seems huge. what's the assumption behind hit rate?
[02:35] Tom: derived from our customers in payments; it assumes standardized instruction prefix for the LLM prompt. if your prompts vary by customer id or dynamic text early, we use normalized templates or canonicalization to boost hits.
[02:48] Samir: normalization is doable, we can strip session IDs in the prefix. question: are there privacy risks storing KV cache? we can't persist raw PII.
[02:58] Tom: KV cache stored encrypted and can be configured ephemeral vs persistent. for regulated workloads we recommend ephemeral or customer-scoped cache in Dedicated/Private with KMS integration. we'll include the KMS flow in the security packet.
[03:12] Priya: and does cache respect tenant isolation? we can't have cross-merchant contamination.
[03:18] Tom: yes, cache keys are namespaced by tenant and model version; isolation is enforced. in Dedicated deployments you can also disable shared caches.
[03:26] Lena: show us the numbers end-to-end — how much cost do we actually save on 1M calls?
[03:32] Tom: in the spreadsheet, scenario A (no cache, small batching) costs $X per 1M tokens; scenario B (65% hit, modest batching) cuts compute tokens by ~40-55% translating to approx 30-45% dollar savings depending on model/instance. exact depends on sequence length distribution.
[03:50] Samir: can we run a bench on our traffic? we'll need sequence length distribution and 24-48h of production traces.
[03:55] Maya: yes, next step is we run a 1-week bench on a sample of your traffic; Tom will give a config and you provide anonymized logs. we can run hosted or a Dedicated pilot.
[04:05] Jorge: what's the effort to enable KV cache in our integration?
[04:09] Tom: it's mostly config: mark the stable prefix region in the prompt or use a library function that splits prompt into prefix and dynamic body. we can share code samples.
[04:18] Samir: are there situations where batching harms quality? like temperature or sampling interactions?
[04:23] Tom: batching is orthogonal to sampling; it just groups concurrent requests. it doesn't change generation outcomes. the only quality risk is when you do aggressive quantization to reduce memory, but we usually recommend testing quantization profiles per workload.
[04:36] Priya: can you reiterate Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for this use case?
[04:40] Maya: Hosted for fastest time-to-value; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and tenant-scoped KV caches plus better audit logs and region pinning — often chosen when customers need strict SLAs and data residency.
[04:52] Lena: we likely need EU residency and SOC2 attestation.
[04:55] Maya: we'll send SOC2 and the security pack after this call. also note our Dedicated offering supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering for private connectivity.
[05:05] Tom: jumping back to cost model — we included a sensitivity table: hit rate vs seq length vs batch window. for example, at 65% hit and 10ms max batching window you still keep p95 ~120ms on typical GPU configs.
[05:20] Jorge: what GPU are you benchmarking on?
[05:22] Tom: A mix — A100-like and newer 80GB runs; for cost modeling we show per-GPU throughput and instance pricing assumptions; we'll tag the sheet with the exact CPU/GPU types.
[05:33] Samir: can caching cause stale context if the prompt changes?
[05:36] Tom: we version cache by prompt hash and model checkpoint; if the prefix template changes, the cache miss occurs and we recompute. TTLs are configurable.
[05:45] Priya: any gotchas around multi-turn chat flows?
[05:48] Tom: multi-turn is a top use case — KV cache shines because the majority of compute is early context. we do need to be mindful of dynamic instructions mid-conversation but we have heuristics to evict or partial match.
[06:00] Maya: quick live demo — Tom, want to share screen and show the spreadsheet and a short trace?
[06:05] Tom: sure sharing. (screen share) top sheet: baseline, then cache scenario. here's the formula for effective tokens saved = hit_rate * prefix_tokens_saved. you can see downstream cost delta.
[06:30] Tom: also showing the config snippet: 
  // pseudo
  const prompt = buildPrompt({prefixTemplate, dynamicFields});
  client.generate({model: 'rwd-13b', prompt, enablePrefixCache: true, tenantId: 'mariner'});
[06:50] Jorge: what about burst windows during settlement at 3AM; will batching hurt peak latency?
[06:58] Tom: for bursts we recommend autoscale + reserved Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput; batching only increases queueing a bit but with reserved capacity you get headroom. we can set per-route policies so critical endpoints avoid long batches.
[07:15] Samir: curious about perf regression detection — if cache reduces tokens but model upgrade causes quality regression, how do we catch?
[07:22] Maya: we integrate with Redwood Optimize evals — you can tie prompt sets and scoring to rollouts. if quality drops we alert and can auto-fallback to previous model.
[07:33] Priya: any security review docs for data at rest for KV cache?
[07:36] Maya: yes included in the security packet: encryption at rest, KMS integration, audit logs for cache access. we'll attach.
[07:45] Lena: okay, can we get a rough timeline for pilot? we want results within two weeks ideally.
[07:51] Tom: typical pilot is 1 week of traffic capture + 3-5 days of benching, so ~2 weeks total.
[07:58] Samir: we'll aim to provide the traces by Monday.
[08:02] Maya: perfect. quick Q/A from Jorge on pricing tiers?
[08:06] Jorge: yeah is there a per-GPU commit for Dedicated and any minimums?
[08:10] Maya: Dedicated starts with a monthly commit; we'll attach the price sheet. for pilots we can run a short-term burst without long term commit.
[08:20] Samir: how do you measure actual token savings in prod to validate model?
[08:24] Tom: our runtime emits token-level metrics per route and cache hit metrics; Optimize ties this into the cost dashboard. you'll get token counts, cache hit rate over time, and cost-per-request.
[08:36] Priya: is that exposed via Console or API?
[08:39] Tom: both — Console has per-route dashboards, and you can query via our metrics API for automation.
[08:46] Maya: logging note — we can anonymize traces on ingest if needed, we accept csv / json exports of sequence lengths and prompt templates.
[08:55] Samir: one more — does cache play nice with function calling / tool use?
[08:59] Tom: yes, the cache is agnostic; for tool-calling flows the prefix still often repeats (tool instructions), so you benefit similarly. just watch for tool outputs in the dynamic portion.
[09:10] Jorge: ok let's talk concrete next steps — restate?
[09:14] Maya: Tom will share the spreadsheet and sample config; I'll share security docs and Dedicated pricing; Mariner will provide anonymized traces; we schedule a follow-up to review bench.
[09:24] Lena: +1. who owns the bench run? us or Redwood?
[09:28] Tom: we can run it in our staging with your anonymized traces or give you the config to run in-house. many customers prefer we run it and share a reproducible report.
[09:38] Priya: we'll prefer Redwood to run it first, then we can replicate on our infra if needed.
[09:42] Maya: sounds good. I'll send calendar invite for follow-up.
[09:45] Jorge: quick question — any hard limits on number of cache entries?
[09:48] Tom: limits depend on deployment and storage tier; we'll show recommended sizing in the doc.
[09:55] Samir: realistic concern: we have lots of small customers with varying prompts, will multi-tenant behavior reduce cache effectiveness across the board?
[09:62] Tom: it's tenant-scoped so each merchant's cache builds independently; for SMBs with noisy prompts hit rates will be lower but batching still helps.
[10:12] Maya: wrap-up — I'll put the links in the follow-up email: security packet (link), pricing sheet (link), KV cache cost model (link).
[10:20] Lena: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[10:22] Maya: thank you all. we'll follow up with action items.
[10:30] (call ends)
